why: I checked both must_not items against the verifier brief, and neither is broken. Item 1: Check 3 lists every exported function at runtime and fails if "any exported function, including subtract (undocumented before this change), has no documentation in README.md". A README that documents clamp but not subtract therefore fails. Item 2: Check 1 tests only behaviour (the clamped results) and never looks at clamp.length. Check 2 tests only `instanceof RangeError`; the message is in the advisory notes, not in PASS/FAIL. Check 3 accepts any documentation ("e.g. a heading or entry naming the function with an explanation"), so it does not require a specific layout. The builder's heading format is guidance, not a verifier condition. Check 4 requires only exit status 0. One borderline point: the note "must include at least add, subtract, multiply and clamp" in Check 3 is stricter than the line's literal wording. I judged it acceptable because it stops the line being met by un-exporting functions, not by adding a format or detail requirement.
